about:
Micron Semiconductor Products Inc. is headquartered in Meridian, Idaho. The company traces its origins to 1978, when a four-person team launched a semiconductor design venture in the basement of a Boise, Idaho dental office. By 1980, the founders had broken ground on their first fabrication plant, and within a few years they introduced the world’s smallest 256K DRAM. The business went public and joined the Fortune 500 in 1994, growing through technology innovations, partnerships, and strategic acquisitions into a global memory and storage manufacturer.

Today Micron designs and manufactures a broad portfolio of memory and storage products, including DRAM components and modules, LPDDR, GDDR, NAND flash, NOR flash, managed NAND, multichip packages, and solid-state drives for data center, client, automotive, and industrial markets. The company operates multiple fabrication facilities and oversees wafer fabrication, assembly, test, and packaging processes. Recent milestones include high-volume production of HBM4 for NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin platform and mass production of its sixth-generation PCIe Gen6 SSD, alongside a 245TB data-center SSD now shipping.

Micron serves customers across automotive, industrial, aerospace and defense, data center and cloud, client PC, consumer electronics, mobile, network infrastructure, industrial IoT, robotics, artificial intelligence, high-performance computing, and video security sectors. Its products are used by original equipment manufacturers, system integrators, hyperscale data-center operators, and automotive Tier 1 suppliers who require high-reliability memory for demanding environments.

The company was founded to advance semiconductor memory technology and has consistently focused on innovation that transforms how information is used. Micron states its purpose is to enrich life for all by delivering optimal memory and storage systems for a wide range of applications, from AI and the cloud to the intelligent edge.
